6.5. Average Value of a Function

6.5 Learning Objectives:

  • I can find the average value of a function on some interval.
  • I can know and understand how to apply the Mean Value Theorem.

Suppose we wanted to find the average of all values that a function 𝑓(𝑥) achieves on an interval [𝑎,𝑏]. We can think about sampling the function at 𝑛 equally spaced points and dividing by the number of points. As we look at sampling more points, we get a more precise approximation for the average of 𝑓.

The approximate function average is

𝑓ave≈𝑓(𝑥1)+𝑓(𝑥2)+…+𝑓(𝑥𝑛)𝑛=1𝑛∑𝑖=1𝑛𝑓(𝑥𝑖)=Δ𝑥𝑏−𝑎∑𝑖=1𝑛𝑓(𝑥𝑖)=1𝑏−𝑎∑𝑖=1𝑛𝑓(𝑥𝑖)Δ𝑥

To make our approximation more accurate, we will sample the function at even more points, eventually taking the limit gives us the integral.

𝑓ave=1𝑏−𝑎lim𝑛→∞∑𝑖=1𝑛𝑓(𝑥𝑖)Δ𝑥=1𝑏−𝑎∫𝑎𝑏𝑓(𝑥)d𝑥.

Solution

We use the formula

𝑓ave=12−(−1)∫−121+𝑥2d𝑥=13[𝑥+𝑥33]−12=13[2+83−(−1−13)]=2

Solution

We use the formula for average of a function

𝑓ave=111−0∫011𝑓(𝑥)d𝑥

In this case, to get the integral, we remember that the integral of a curve is the same as the area under that curve. We don’t need the equation for 𝑓 since we can use geometry to find the area.

Now, we add the areas of the different parts up: 𝐴1=12𝜋𝑟2=12𝜋42=8𝜋 And 𝐴2=𝑤ℎ=(8)(3)=24. And 𝐴3=12𝑏ℎ=12(3)(3)=92.

Then, the average is

𝑓ave=111∫011𝑓(𝑥)d𝑥=111(𝐴1+𝐴2+𝐴3)=111(8𝜋+24+92).

Solution

Yes, because 𝑓 is continuous (since it is a polynomial), so by Mean Value Theorem (MVT) the function achieves its average value for some 𝑐 in (𝑎,𝑏).

As for where this happens, the MVT does not say. We can find it though,

𝑓ave=12−0∫02(𝑥+1)3d𝑥=12∫13𝑢3d𝑢=12𝑢44|13=12(344−14)=10

Where the 𝑢-sub we used was 𝑢=𝑥+1 so d𝑢=d𝑥 and 𝑢(0)=1 and 𝑢(2)=3.

Since the average value is now known (10), we can find which 𝑐 value has 𝑓(𝑐)=10.

10=(𝑐+1)3103=𝑐+1103−1=𝑐

which is in (0,2).

6.5 Section Summary:

  • We found the average value of a function on some interval.
  • We used mean value theorem to find where a function achieves its average value.
